sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2016 Fiat 500C Abarth Cabriolet, finished in Nero with a Nero soft top and a Nero interior. The attached Carfax vehicle history report shows no mileage discrepancies in this 500C’s past; it also shows registrations in Florida and Texas since new. According to the build sheet provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes 17-inch forged aluminum wheels, a power-retractable soft top, leather upholstery, and an Alpine sound system. The seller reports no notable modifications. The fixed-profile convertible variant of the 500 debuted at the Geneva Motor Show in March 2009. It was designated as the 500C, recalling the fixed-profile convertible of the original 1957 Fiat 500. The hot-rodded Abarth-tuned model offered numerous performance-oriented upgrades, including a more powerful engine, a firmer suspension, and bigger brakes. Production for the American market ended after the 2019 model year. Power comes from a 1.4-liter turbocharged inline-4, rated at 160 horsepower and 170 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the front wheels via a 6-speed automatic transmission.
